mappings.note: Blow over rubbed peanuts and report which component leaves. A conducted separation with the observation to be made, LO-95.
Dry salt solution on black paper, then say what the patches are and where the water went. An investigation whose inference the student must draw, LO-95.
Boil the solution in a china dish and check whether the salt is recovered. A conducted separation with a result to report, LO-95.
Run the filtration and report that mud stays as residue while clear filtrate collects below. A conducted investigation, LO-95.
Design and BUILD a working water filter for Valli's pond water. LO-100 for constructing a working model from available materials, LO-103 because the design is the student's own.
Sort separation examples into two baskets by PURPOSE -- removing an unwanted component or recovering a useful one. A classification of processes, LO-94.
Hand-picking serves the purpose of sorting. Placing a method in its functional category, LO-94.
Cream from milk is separated by churning. Matching a household separation to its method, LO-101, whose own example is separating materials.
Pore size is what governs filtration. The item asks what the outcome DEPENDS on, so the cause, LO-96.
Five true/false claims each pairing a mixture with a method, with corrections. Sorting mixtures to the right separation method, LO-94.
When to decant rather than filter. An explicit differentiation of two methods by when each works, LO-93.
Nasal hair as a natural filter. Recognising a separation process in the body, LO-101.
What masks are made of and what they do. Filtration applied to an everyday health practice, LO-101.
A stepwise plan to separate potatoes, salt and sawdust. Chaining several methods to solve a real separation, LO-101's own example.
Choose the right word at each step of Leela's water-purification story. Applying the methods to a practical sequence, LO-101.
What handpicking is -- removing components by hand on visible differences. Explaining a process, LO-97.
What Nani's community was handpicking out of the grain. A separation observed in everyday village life, LO-101.
When handpicking is convenient -- few, large, visually distinct particles. The conditions that make a method work, LO-96.
What threshing is -- beating grain free of the stalks. Explaining a process, LO-97.
What happens when rubbed peanuts are blown on. Explaining the separation that results, LO-97; the activity version got LO-95.
Winnowing works on the weight difference. The principle a method rests on, LO-96.
What sieving is for -- solid-solid mixtures differing in size. Explaining a process, LO-97.
How common salt is won from seawater in shallow pits. Evaporation applied at industrial scale in daily supply, LO-101.
What Activity 9.2 leaves on the dark paper. Recall of the conducted activity's result, LO-95.
What sedimentation is -- heavier insoluble solids settling. Explaining a process, LO-97.
Dada's method for tea without a strainer -- let the leaves settle, then pour off. A household separation, LO-101.
Why decantation leaves some leaves behind -- finer ones stay suspended or pour over. The cause of an incomplete separation, LO-96.
What filtration is -- insoluble solids held back by a filter. Explaining a process, LO-97.
Filter paper, with very fine pores, outperforms cloth. Identifying a material by the feature that makes it work, LO-92.
How filtration differs from sieving -- solid from liquid against solid from solid. An explicit differentiation of two processes, LO-93.
A fishing net works like a filter. Recognising the principle in an unrelated everyday practice, LO-101.
What churning is used for -- butter out of curd or cream. Explaining a process, LO-97.
Why butter rises and buttermilk stays below during churning. The density cause of the separation, LO-96.
WHY a magnet separates iron nails from sawdust -- one is magnetic, the other is not. The property that causes the separation, LO-96.
What magnetic separation is. Explaining a process, LO-97.
The soop, a bamboo winnowing tray. Identifying a tool by name and appearance, LO-92. Option (B) has been corrupted into a figure caption.
The main DIFFERENCE between threshing and winnowing. An explicit differentiation of two processes, LO-93. Option (D) is truncated with its tail in the stem.
Which method will NOT recover salt and water from a solution -- filtration. Tests which method belongs to which kind of mixture, LO-94.
Recover sugar from a sand-sugar mixture by dissolving, filtering and evaporating. Chaining methods to solve a real separation, LO-101.
Assertion-reason: sieving separates flour from bran BECAUSE of the particle-size difference. The causal clause is what is marked, LO-96.
Mami sieving coarse particles from flour before kneading. Choosing the right method for a kitchen task, LO-101.

Kabir's doha, where the soop keeps the grain and lets the husk fly -- an image for keeping virtues and discarding vices. Cited at LO-104, which carries the values of honesty and freedom from prejudice, since the couplet's point is moral.
Why stones must come out of grain before cooking. The everyday reason a separation is worth doing, LO-101.
Pouring off the liquid after settling is decantation. Naming a process, LO-97.
Why medicinal herbs are shade-dried -- slow evaporation of water concentrates the active parts. The reason behind a practice, LO-96. The Ayurveda reference is corrupted to 'Arrived' in the stem.
Residue against filtrate. An explicit differentiation of the two products of filtration, LO-93.
Which method is LEAST effective for oil and water -- sieving. Tests which method suits which kind of mixture, LO-94.
Separating pebbles from sand for mortar, by handpicking or sieving depending on quantity. Choosing a method for a real job, LO-101.
Assertion-reason on threshers doing both jobs, beating then blowing. Explaining how the combined process works, LO-97.

Which listed activities are separations -- handpicking peppers and threshing, but not kneading. Tests the boundary of what counts as separation, LO-94. Only the last of the three numbered items survives in the stem.
Name the settling step and the pouring step for chalk in water. Naming two linked processes, LO-97.
Why salt vanishes in water while sand stays visible. Solubility as the cause, LO-96.
The solid caught on the filter is the residue. Naming what is observed, LO-92.
Farmers beating wheat stalks on a log, which is threshing. Recognising a process from what is observed, LO-97.
Why winnowing fails in a closed room -- no air current. The condition a method depends on, LO-96.
What threshers are -- machines doing threshing and winnowing together. Explaining a process as mechanised, LO-97.
Mami removing bran from flour by sieving. A kitchen separation and its method, LO-101.
How the particles passing through compare with those retained. The size relation that makes sieving work, LO-96.
Which method is LEAST suitable for tea leaves -- evaporation. Tests which method fits which mixture, LO-94.
Getting clear water from settled chalk by decanting or filtering. Choosing the method for a practical goal, LO-101.
